summary: Hugh Edward Richardson was a Tibetologist who studied at Keble College, Oxford (~1923–1927). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1930–1947), was a visiting professor at the University of Washington (~1959–1961), and founded the Tibet Society and the Institute of Tibetan Studies.

Hugh Falconer worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the universities of Aberdeen (~1822–1826) and Edinburgh (~1826–1829), later serving as Superintendent of Saharanpur Botanical Garden (1832) and Calcutta Medical College Professor of Botany (1848–1855).

Hugh George Rawlinson worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. After earning an M.A. at Emmanuel College (~1899–1903), he served in the Ceylon Educational Service (1903), Karnatak Arts College (1917–1923), and Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1919–1933).
Hugh Gray worked in Indology and other fields. Educated at Battersea Grammar School, he served as a lecturer at the University of London and held a post at SOAS University of London (~1960–1983).

Hugh J. Silverman was a philosopher who completed his doctorate at Stanford University (~1969–1973). He was a professor at Stony Brook University from 1974 and served as executive director of the International Association for Philosophy and Literature (~1976–2013).

Hugh Trevor Lambrick worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned his B.A. (~1923–1927) and D.Litt. (1971) at Oxford, served as President of the Sind Historical Society (1940–1943), and became a Fellow and Lecturer at Oriel College.

Hugh van Skyhawk is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Günther-Dietz Sontheimer. In 2008, he held a post as Professor of Comparative Religion in the Taxila Institute of Asian Civilizations at Quaid-i-Azam University.

Hugo David is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at EPHE (PhD 2012), Sciences Po Grenoble, and Sciences Po. He held a fellowship at Cambridge (2013–2014) and became a permanent member of the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2015.

Hugo Ehrlich was a linguist who studied at the University of Jena (~1897–1898) and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Leipzig under Karl Brugmann (~1898–1901). In 1912, he was a Privatdozent in Indo-European linguistics at the University of Königsberg.

Hugo Enomiya-Lassalle was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He held a post at Sophia University (~1935–1945) and studied under the traditional teacher Koun Yamada (~1970–1989).

Hugo Heinrich Figulla was a linguist and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Breslau under Bruno Meissner (~1908–1911). He held positions at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1934–1936) and served as Keeper at the British Museum (1946–1963).

Hugo Schuchardt was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Bonn under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl (~1861–1864). He taught at Halle-Wittenberg (1873) and served as ordinary professor of Romance Philology at the University of Graz (1876–1900).
Hugo Valvanne was an Indology scholar who completed his M.A. studies under J. N. Reuter at the University of Helsinki (~1912–1917).
Hugo Winckler was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1882–1886) and later held an academic post there (~1891–1913).
Huidi Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yi-hsun Huang (attested 2011).
Huifeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2007) and held a post at the University of Hong Kong.

Huimin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1986–1992). He served as a professor at Taipei National University of the Arts (~1992–2014) and as President of Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts (~2014–2022).
Huishan Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under Kuo-wei Liu, also studying under Mansheng, Miaoguan, and Ruying.
Huiwen Zhuang is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University supervised by Kirill Solonin, having also studied under the traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Huiyu Zhang is an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held an attested post as a lecturer at Dongguk University in 1996.
